It embodies the inter-city rivalry between [[Bilbao]] and [[San Sebastián|Donostia-San Sebastián]], respectively the capitals of the neighbouring provinces of [[Biscay]] (''Bizkaia'') and [[Gipuzkoa]] in the [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]] region of Spain.{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/five-things-you-need-to-know-about-the-basque-derby|title=Five things you need to know about... the Basque derby|publisher=[[Liga de Fútbol Profesional]]|date=11 March 2017 |access-date=30 August 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.thenational.ae/sport/primera-liga/for-david-moyes-in-basque-derby-identity-and-sovreignty-and-points-all-part-of-the-pressure |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150928201010/http://www.thenational.ae/sport/primera-liga/for-david-moyes-in-basque-derby-identity-and-sovreignty-and-points-all-part-of-the-pressure |url-status=dead |archive-date=28 September 2015 |title=For David Moyes in Basque derby, identity and sovereignty and points all part of the pressure |newspaper=[[The National (Abu Dhabi)|The National]] |date=25 September 2015 |access-date=21 November 2017}} It is also occasionally referred to as the [[Autopista AP-8|AP-8]] derby, referring to the name of the highway which connects the cities. ==Background== The derby was first played in April 1909 and has attracted the attention of local football fans ever since. These two organisations are the largest football clubs in the Basque Country and have stayed in the top division of Spanish football for longer than most clubs, winning several trophies in the last hundred years. Both enjoyed a period of great success in the early 1980s, winning four [[La Liga|national titles]] in succession between them, whilst [[Athletic Bilbao signing policy|using only local players]].{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2002/08/13/liga/1029227781.html|title=Boris, primer español no vasco en la Real |trans-title=Boris, first non-Basque Spaniard at Real |language=es|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|date=13 August 2002|access-date=12 February 2018}} Other clubs in the territory have also competed in the top division (and opposed Real Sociedad occasionally in the second tier, in addition to cup ties), with [[CA Osasuna]], [[Deportivo Alavés]], and [[SD Eibar]] the most prominent of these; the matches between any of them are also referred to as a “[[Basque football derbies|Basque derby]]”.{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/osasuna-vs-ath-bilbao/210358|title=All square in Basque derby |publisher=Sky Sports|date=26 April 2010|access-date=16 December 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.gasteizhoy.com/el-alaves-se-lleva-el-derby-ante-el-athletic/|title=El Alavés se lleva el derby ante el Athletic|trans-title=Alavés takes the derby against Athletic|newspaper=Gasteiz Hoy|language=es|date=7 May 2017|access-date=30 August 2017}}{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2017/02/28/actualidad/1488307346_053812.html|title=Real Sociedad-Eibar: Un derbi 'in extremis' |trans-title=Real Sociedad-Eibar: A derby 'in extremis'|newspaper=El País|language=es|date=28 February 2017|access-date=30 August 2017|last1=Rodrigálvarez |first1=Eduardo }} [[File:Erreala athletic derby 0001.jpg|thumb|left|Rival supporters socialising together pre-match in San Sebastián, October 2011]] Supporters of both teams traditionally mix in and around the stadiums on matchdays,{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/us/features/basque-bone-why-athletic-bilbao-vs-real-sociedad-more-game?page=0%2C3|title=Basque to the bone? Athletic Bilbao has never been relegated,{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11096/10880323/athletic-bilbaos-methods-provide-lessons-for-premier-league-clubs|title=Athletic Bilbao's methods provide lessons for Premier League clubs|publisher=Sky Sports|date=18 May 2017|access-date=26 December 2017}} meaning all their league matches have taken place in the top tier. In the 21st century, there has only been one enforced break in the fixtures, a three-year (1400 days) hiatus between January 2007 and December 2010.{{cite web|url=http://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/noticias/2010-12-05/derbi-disputa-desde-mediodia-20101205.html|title=El derbi se disputa desde el mediodía|trans-title=The derby is disputed from noon|publisher=El Diario Vasco|language=es|date=5 December 2010|access-date=17 December 2017|archive-date=14 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214115011/https://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/noticias/2010-12-05/derbi-disputa-desde-mediodia-20101205.html|url-status=dead}} ==History== ===1900s cups=== [[File:Club Ciclista Campeonato-de-España 1909.jpg|thumb|The [[Club Ciclista de San Sebastián]] team with the [[1909 Copa del Rey]]]] The first meeting between Athletic Bilbao and a team which evolved into Real Sociedad should have taken place in the [[1905 Copa del Rey]], which consisted of a mini-league with just three teams: Athletic, hosts [[Real Madrid C.F.|Madrid F.C.]] and [[San Sebastián Recreation Club]].{{cite web|url=http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/Copa05.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030910160133/http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/Copa05.htm |url-status=usurped |archive-date=10 September 2003 |title=Copa del Rey Alfonso XIII 1905|trans-title=Cup of King Alfonso XIII 1905|language=es|website=LinguaSport|access-date=14 December 2017}} After Madrid defeated both Basque teams, Athletic declined to play the [[dead rubber]] between them. Despite this withdrawal, however, the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation|federation]] considers Athletic to be the runners-up in the tournament as it was their match with Madrid which confirmed the latter as the winners. By the [[1909 Copa del Rey|1909 event]], the ''Recreation Club'' had evolved into ''San Sebastián Foot-Ball Club'' but aligned with [[Club Ciclista de San Sebastián]] to meet the entry requirements.{{cite web|url=http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/Copa09.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120113051909/http://www.linguasport.com/FUTBOL/nacional/copa/Copa09.htm |url-status=usurped |archive-date=13 January 2012 |title=Copa del Rey Alfonso XIII 1909|trans-title=Cup of King Alfonso XIII 1909|language=es|website=LinguaSport|access-date=14 December 2017}} They defeated Athletic in the opening round and went on to win the trophy.{{cite news|url=http://gara.naiz.eus/paperezkoa/20090906/155280/es/Un-siglo-futbol-club-ciclista-origen|title=Un siglo de fútbol con el club ciclista como origen|trans-title=A century of football with a cycling club as its origin|language=es|publisher=Gara|date=6 June 2009|access-date=16 December 2017}}{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2009/08/15/mas_futbol/1250317621_850215.html|title=Todo empezó en el Club Ciclista San Sebastián...|trans-title=It all started at the Club Ciclista San Sebastián...|language=es|publisher=Diario AS|date=15 August 2009|access-date=14 December 2017}}{{cite news|url=http://www.diariovasco.com/v/20140409/deportes/mas-futbol/cumplen-anos-primer-titulo-20140409.html|title=Se cumplen 105 años del primer título de Copa donostiarra que conquistó el Club Ciclista|trans-title=It is 105 years since the San Sebastian's first cup win, conquered by Club Ciclista|language=es|publisher=El Diario Vasco|date=9 April 2014|access-date=14 December 2017}} [[File:Athletic 1910.jpg|thumb|left|Athletic Bilbao's [[1910 Copa del Rey]]-winning team]] The [[1910 Copa del Rey|following year]], the club was renamed ''Sociedad de Foot-Ball de San Sebastián'' and had received royal patronage, entitling it to add the prefix ''Real''. cumpliría hoy cien años|trans-title=Old San Mamés would be 100 years old today|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=es|date=21 August 2013|access-date=14 December 2017}} In the same year, regional league competitions were introduced to the area to determine the qualifying teams for the [[Copa del Rey]]. In the first three seasons, Athletic Bilbao and Real Sociedad were in the same competition, but due to repeated disputes by the rival provinces, these separated into the [[Biscay Championship]] – dominated by Athletic and [[Arenas Club de Getxo]] – and the [[Gipuzkoa Championship]] – usually won by Real Sociedad or [[Real Unión]] – which ran in parallel for sixteen years. In 1934 the top six clubs in the region, including Athletic and Real (then known as ''Donostia FC'' under the [[Second Spanish Republic]] which rejected regal names), were involved in the ''Basque Cup'' which ran until 1936 when the [[Spanish Civil War]] brought an end to organised football for three years. At the end of the conflict, the regional championships were re-instated for two further seasons, with ''Atlético de Bilbao'' (another renaming, this time an order of [[Francoist Spain|Franco's regime]] prohibiting non-Spanish words that lasted until the 1970s) and Real Sociedad kept apart. By then, the national league was well established, with the clubs' first meeting in that competition occurring in February 1929.{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/derby-stats-and-curiosities-of-the-basque-derby|title=Derby stats and curiosities of the Basque derby|publisher=[[Liga de Fútbol Profesional]]|date=4 January Basque derby == Athletic Bilbao established [[Athletic Club Femenino|their women's team]] in 2002, with [[Real Sociedad Femenino|that of Real Sociedad]] founded two years later and reaching the top tier in 2006. While Athletic have won the [[Primera División (women)|national league title]] on five occasions, Real have yet to be champions, although they have never been relegated from the top division and in 2019 were winners of the [[Copa de la Reina de Fútbol|Copa de la Reina]], which Athletic had never been able to
